the post-natally developing thymus is capable of developing in the absence of daily bone marrow input, and this is modeled by a four-compartment mathematical model that includes a decrease of the proliferation rate as the main factor for the involution of the mouse thymocyte population.

the model is able to describe the dynamics of the main thymocyte subpopulations during the development of the thymic epithelium, from the emergence in the fetal stage to death of the animal in the post-natal stage.

(i) a four-compartment mathematical model can be used to describe the development of the mouse thymocytes from the fetal to the adult stage and (ii) the post-natal development of thymocyte populations can be explained without taking into account the input of bone marrow derived progenitors.

a mathematical model that can explain the dynamics of thymocyte populations from the fetal to the post-natal stages, and the role of the bone marrow in the post-natal stage.

the post-natally developing thymus is autonomous and that it does not require bone marrow progenitors for the development of its main thymocyte subpopulations.

the post-natally developing mouse thymus is not only capable of maintaining itself, but it is able to develop without the daily input of new bone marrow progenitors and that this process is not dependent on a continuous input of new cells from the bone marrow.
